title: Compact stream framing, priority lanes, and SDK patterns
summary: Exploratory PRD sketch proposing a compact framing protocol for incremental streaming responses with explicit client-side priority lanes, a tooling hedging model for speculative tool calls, and SDK ergonomics for backpressure and partial structured output handling.
goals:
1) Define a compact, byte-efficient frame format for partial responses that encodes priority, type, and optional structured payloads.
2) Surface a small, ergonomic SDK API so client apps can declare priorities and fallback policies and easily consume partial structured outputs.
3) Introduce a speculative tool-call hedging model to reduce tail latency for tool invocations without blowing up request cost.
4) Provide a staged rollout plan and compatibility guidance for existing streaming endpoints.
non_goals: Not proposing a full wire-compatible replacement for the existing event-stream (SSE/HTTP2 chunking); not locking into a single serialization format for structured payloads (will support JSON and newline-delimited JSON initially).
user_stories:
- As a conversational agent engineer, I want low-latency incremental tokens for short user messages but higher-fidelity structured data for tool outputs.
- As a mobile client developer, I want to mark certain responses as high-priority so they arrive before background analytics tokens.
- As an SDK consumer, I want an easy way to resume a partially received response after a transient network hiccup.
- As a platform engineer, I want observability hooks for per-frame drop/retry and per-tool hedging metrics.
design-overview:
We propose layering a compact framing protocol on top of HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming. Frames are small header+payload units. Header is fixed 1-2 bytes for common flags (frame type, priority lane, continuation flag) plus a variable-length length field. Types include: CHUNK (text token or token delta), STRUCT (structured JSON output), TOOL_CALL (tool invocation request/response metadata), CHECKPOINT (resumable anchors), and HEARTBEAT. Priority lanes (0-3) are encoded with two bits; clients can tag outgoing requests with a default lane and provide per-call overrides. The server can reorder and emit frames across lanes; the SDK exposes an ordering guarantee per-lane (strict) and relaxed ordering across lanes.
Key features: compact header to reduce token overhead for mobile; explicit checkpoint frames to support resumability; structured frames that carry schema identifiers; and tool-call frames that include hedging hints and confidence scores.
Backward compatibility: server accepts a legacy streaming flag; if client does not speak compact framing, server falls back to current SSE-like behavior and emits translated frames until the stream can be upgraded.
protocol-framing:
Frame header layout (proposal):
- 1 byte: flags (bits: 0-1 priority, 2-4 frame type, 5 continuation, 6 reserved, 7 compressed)
- varint: payload length (LEB128)
- payload bytes
Frame types (3-bit): 0=CHUNK, 1=STRUCT, 2=TOOL_CALL, 3=TOOL_RESP, 4=CHECKPOINT, 5=HEARTBEAT, 6=METADATA, 7=RESERVED
Example flows:
- Incremental text: CHUNK frames, priority=0 (low) for background telemetry; priority=3 (high) for immediate assistant replies.
- Tool call: TOOL_CALL frame from server => SDK may open a separate tool channel or allow inline TOOL_RESP frames; hedging hint inside TOOL_CALL suggests estimated latency distribution.
Resumability: CHECKPOINT frames contain a monotonic stream cursor (opaque string) plus optional KV of small state blobs (base64). Clients can request resume with last-seen cursor; server validates and emits delta frames.
Compression: flag bit for payload-level compression; negotiation via initial headers.
Security: frames are emitted over TLS; ensure length prefix prevents over-read; any reserved bits default to zero for forward compatibility.
sdk-ergonomics:
Surface two high-level client APIs: StreamReader (push model) and StreamIterator (pull model).
- StreamReader.on('frame', (frame) => { ... }) with typed helpers: frame.asText(), frame.asJson(schema?), frame.asToolResponse().
- StreamIterator for async iteration: for await (const frame of stream.iter()) { ... }
Priority API: request = client.createRequest(prompt, { priority: 'high' | 'med' | 'low', lanes: {response:2, telemetry:0} });
Backpressure: SDK exposes ability to signal available buffer capacity (credits) to server; simple token-based credit window (clientCredit = N frames). Server automatically slows lower-priority lanes if client credit exhausted.
Tool hedging: SDK can opt into tool hedging policy with two knobs: maxSpeculativeCalls (0-2) and costBudget (ms or token-equivalent). The server will launch speculative calls to warm tool endpoints and cancel lower-confidence duplicates when a fast response arrives.
Resuming: client stores last checkpoint ID to durable storage and can call client.resumeStream(checkpointId). SDK will surface resumable checkpoints as application-level events.
Developer ergonomics: provide clear typed bindings (TS types), small helpers for common patterns (collectUntilCheckpoint, assembleStructuredPayload), and a debug flag that prints frame-level timeline for logs.
rollout-plan:
Phase 0: internal alpha (sdk + server opt-in flag) for partner teams only; collect telemetry for frame rates and size distribution.
Phase 1: beta for public customers with opt-in header; SDKs publish v0.9 with feature flags.
Phase 2: default-on for new SDKs, existing clients remain on legacy protocol until migration window closes (6 months).
Phase 3: deprecation notice for older streaming mode; full enforcement after 9-12 months.
Metrics to monitor: frames/sec, avg frame size, checkpoint frequency, resume success rate, speculative tool duplicate calls per minute, hedging cost delta, tail latency p95/p99 for tool responses.
open-questions:
- What are safe defaults for priority lanes and client credit to avoid starvation of low priority traffic?
- How to reliably map structured schema identifiers across models and downstream connectors?
- Hedging cost model: how to expose estimated token/cost impact to customers and enforce tenant-level cost budgets?
- Edge-case: how to handle long-lived checkout streams where checkpoints grow large (exceeding 4KB) — truncate or compress?
- Mobile/IoT: should SDK include an offline replay queue to respawn resumed streams when connectivity returns?
